structure.title: An edict and a decision
structure.text: The opening sets a ruler's command against a sister's obligation, making a private burial a public challenge.

structure.title: Refusing correction
structure.text: Successive encounters test whether authority can hear opposition without interpreting it as disloyalty.

people.name: Antigone
people.text: The daughter of Oedipus, who resolves to bury her brother Polynices against the king's order, because she holds the gods' law above any man's.

people.name: Creon
people.text: Antigone's uncle, newly king of Thebes after a civil war, who forbids the burial of a traitor to show that the city's law must be obeyed.

people.name: Ismene
people.text: Antigone's cautious sister, who loves her as much as she fears the king, and refuses at first to break the law beside her.

context.title: Burial and obligation
context.text: Burial gives the dead religious and familial recognition. Denying it asserts authority beyond the dead person's defeat in battle.
context.takeaway: The body is not merely a political symbol.

context.title: After civil conflict
context.text: The city needs order after violence within its ruling family. Creon's wish to establish authority therefore has an intelligible public purpose.
context.takeaway: Understand the purpose without accepting every means.

notice.text: Notice who equates disagreement with corruption.
notice.why: The suspicion makes advice increasingly difficult to hear.

notice.text: Compare the sisters' ideas of loyalty.
notice.why: Shared affection does not produce identical choices.

opening: Antigone's brother has been declared a traitor, and the new ruler forbids anyone to bury him. Leaving his body exposed will demonstrate that the city has a government again. Antigone intends to bury him anyway. Both understand the public meaning of what they are doing, and neither thinks the other has the right to decide. Sophocles brings political authority into collision with an obligation that cannot be voted away, while a ruler's need to appear firm steadily narrows his ability to hear advice.
